name: read_file
description: Read the contents of one file inside the workspace. The only way this runtime is permitted to learn what a file contains — nothing infers or guesses file content from a name, an extension, or what such a file typically holds.

path.description: Path to the file, relative to the workspace root. Absolute paths and any path resolving outside the workspace root are refused.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-indexed). Omit to start at the top. Use with `limit` to page through a file too large to read in one call.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Omit to read to the end of the file, subject to `max_bytes`.

encoding.description: Text encoding to decode the file as. A file that fails to decode under the requested encoding returns an error rather than best-effort mangled text.

path.description: The resolved, workspace-relative path actually read.

content.description: The file's text, for the requested range.

truncated.description: True if `limit` or `max_bytes` cut the result short of the file's full content. A truncated read must never be treated as the whole file.

total_lines.description: Total line count in the file, independent of what was returned.

byte_size.description: Size of the file on disk, in bytes.

errors.description: No file exists at the resolved path.
The path resolves to a directory, not a file.
The path resolves outside the workspace root and was refused before any filesystem access was attempted.
The file does not decode as text under the requested encoding — likely a binary asset. Returned rather than guessed at.
The file exceeds this runtime's single-read size ceiling. Retry with `offset`/`limit` to page through it.

safety_notes: Read-only and side-effect-free: this tool never creates, modifies, or deletes anything, and never executes file content. Path resolution happens before any filesystem call is made, so `outside_workspace` is a refusal, not a failed attempt. A caller that needs to confirm a file exists before acting on it should call this tool rather than assuming — CLAUDE.md's rule against fabricating file contents applies to every consumer of this schema, not only to the reference implementation.
